segments.name: Flexible friends planning a cheap escape
Flexible couple seeking a cheap short break

population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

rounds.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

decision.reason: The member fare of 376 HKD is a genuinely cheap escape that turns a flexible, unplanned break into a real trip, and I have not travelled for six months. Although KIX has little particular pull today, the group is open on destination and this price makes the optional outing worthwhile. I would still pay the 470 HKD normal fare if the member quota ran out.

analysis.summary: 16 members responded at a 376 HKD member fare. Eight bought the member fare, citing strong value and price sensitivity; eight declined, of whom four were blocked by budget or availability and four cited low trip interest or optional-leisure inertia rather than the fare itself. No customer objected to the price as too high. The current fare sits at the permitted cap, so buying at 376 HKD does not establish willingness to pay more. Evidence supports testing the same fare on fresh customers rather than moving it.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 376 HKD member fare on fresh members will reproduce roughly 40-50% weighted conversion, with declines driven mainly by low trip interest and budget or availability constraints rather than fare objections. A materially lower conversion would contradict this.

analysis.summary: Six of sixteen members bought at the 376 HKD fare, citing strong value and destination appeal; several said they would also pay the 470 regular fare. Five declines were inventory/budget-forced, and four were low interest, low destination appeal, or optional-trip preference rather than price objections. No customer rejected the fare as too expensive. The fare sits at the permitted cap, so no higher test is allowed. Evidence supports retaining the current fare for a fresh paired test.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 376 HKD member fare on fresh members will reproduce conversion near the observed 40%, with declines driven mainly by availability and low trip interest rather than fare level; a materially lower conversion would contradict this.

analysis.summary: At the current 270 HKD member fare, 9 of 16 customers bought and 7 declined. All declines cite low trip interest or optional-leisure preference, not price; one decline is environment-forced. Several buyers explicitly say they would not pay the 470 regular fare, while others would. No customer objects to the fare itself, and no inventory denials occurred. Evidence suggests demand is driven by the low fare for price-sensitive buyers, but declines are not price-driven, so a directional price test is weakly supported.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce conversion enough to lower basic receipts, because current buyers include several who state willingness to pay the 470 regular fare.

analysis.summary: Of 15 members, 4 bought the 364 HKD member fare and 11 declined. Six declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), not price objections; five were low trip interest or recent travel, i.e. optional-trip appeal rather than fare. Only the buyers cite the fare as decisive, and two would pay 470 while two would not. No decline attributes its decision to the fare level, so the evidence does not support lowering price; the current fare sits below the 376 cap with quota and seats unconstrained.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh members will not reduce weighted conversion enough to lower basic ticket receipts, because current buyers include two willing to pay 470 and declines are driven by availability or trip interest rather than fare.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the 333 HKD member fare, 9 of 16 customers bought and 7 declined. Four declines were inventory/budget-forced with no available basic fare, and three were low-interest optional browsing rather than price objections. Buyers repeatedly called 333 a standout bargain; two said they would not pay 470. No decline cited the fare as too high. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at 333 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce member conversion enough to lower basic ticket receipts, because current buyers describe 333 as unusually cheap and several would still pay 470.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: Six of sixteen members bought at the 376 HKD fare, all citing the fare itself as the decisive trigger; several would also pay the 470 regular fare. Five declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and five were low-interest optional browsing where price was called affordable but not motivating. No customer objected to price as too high. The current fare sits at the permitted cap, so evidence supports retaining it rather than raising it.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 376 HKD fare on fresh members will reproduce conversion near one-third, with declines driven mainly by low trip interest or unavailable inventory rather than fare level; a materially lower conversion would contradict this.

Four declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and three declines cited low destination or trip interest rather than price. No customer objected to the fare level itself. The current price sits below the 376 HKD cap, and evidence points to strong value perception rather than price resistance.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce member conversion enough to lower basic ticket receipts, since buyers reported willingness to pay the 470 HKD regular fare and no decline cited price as the main reason.
